---
title: Introduction
---

`ambdes` is an open-source discrete-event simulation (DES) ambulance demand and resources. It can explore how changes in demand, ambulance capacity and operational delays may affect response performance. It is being developed as a prototype with South Western Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust (SWASFT).

The model represents incidents in four response capacities:

* **C1** - life-threatening incidents
* **C2** - emergency incidents
* **C3** - urgent incidents
* **C4** - less urgent incidents

It is limited to calls that receive an in-person responses (and so includes hear-and-treat, which are cases managed over the phone). These incidents are either:

* **See-and-treat** - ambulance attends and treats on scene.
* **See-and-convey** - ambulance attends, treats on scene, and then conveys to a destination (e.g., to hospital).

It's main performance measure is **mean response time**, with results available by response category and response outcome (i.e., conveyed or not). It also reports resource utilisation.
